script: That's My Table!. Last summer I had some time to kill while the car was being worked on and went to a fast food restaurant. It was a quiet afternoon, no one else in the place. The layout was a grid of 4 rows and 5 tables, all identical, all with the same number of chairs. Twenty tables total. I ordered, slid into a spot, and started munching. A man walked in a few minutes later, ordered, and took a seat at the far end of the room. That left 18 identical, empty tables. I was half through my meal, feeling the day slip by, when a family burst in. They ordered, and a kid—maybe 8 or 10—strolled toward me. "Hey, lady, you're going to have to move. That's our table, we always sit there," he said. I ignored him. (I know, right?) Then it hit me when the kid's dad approached, staring straight at me. He didn't correct his kid; instead he told me the same line, "We always sit at that table." I ignored him, too. (Literally insane.) They took the seat right next to mine and started creeping into my personal space, glancing at me every time they bumped a chair. I could feel their eyes on me. I purposely slowed my bites, savoring each chew to make them feel the sting of my irritation. Their glare was a constant reminder that they thought they owned the place. I could feel the tension building, like a slow-motion car crash. I waited until they finished, then got up, slid out of the chair, and left before they could even think of moving. I was leaving, but their stare followed me. The air felt heavy as I walked out, and I couldn't help but wonder if the audacity of their claim was really that big. The moment I stepped onto the sidewalk, my mind was still stuck in that cramped space…
